title: An over-long line still reaches QuickBooks Online and matches the report
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a test location whose QuickBooks Online connection is active, linked to a QuickBooks sandbox company you can sign in to.
  • Make sure Require Tech Story is off (Settings, then the Work Orders tab).
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with one labor line, line 1, titled "Replace tie rods" (16 characters) whose description is the letter é written 3,000 times in a row (paste it in).
  • Have line 1 completed with no tech story, and work order 1 completed and invoiced today as invoice A, which the QuickBooks sync picks up.
  • Write down invoice A's number.
  • Use Google Sheets (File, then Import, then Upload) to open downloaded files, so accented letters and character counts read correctly.
  • Keep the QuickBooks sandbox company open in a second browser tab.
  • Start on Reports, then Export Reports in the Reports left menu, with the Export Report dialog open.
custom_steps:
1. In the QuickBooks tab, search for invoice A's number.
  2. Open invoice A.
  3. Copy line 1's Description into cell A1 of a new Google Sheet.
  4. In cell B1, enter =LEN(A1).
  5. Switch to the ShopView tab.
  6. Click QB Unexported in the Reports left menu.
  7. Click Export Reports in the Reports left menu.
  8. Pick Customer Invoice in the Report Name list.
  9. Set the date range to today.
  10. Click Download.
  11. Open the downloaded file in Google Sheets.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • QuickBooks lists invoice A, work order 1's invoice: the over-long line did not stop it from syncing.

Step 2:

  • Invoice A opens; line 1's Description starts with "Replace tie rods - é" and ends with a whole é.

Step 3:

  • Cell A1 holds the Description.

Step 4:

  • Cell B1 shows 2009 (16 + 3 + 1,990 letters é, the most that fit in the 4,000 limit).

Step 5:

  • The ShopView tab is in front, on Reports.

Step 6:

  • The QB Unexported list opens on its Customers tab, and invoice A is not in it.

Step 7:

  • The Export Report dialog opens.

Step 8:

  • Customer Invoice is picked in Report Name.

Step 9:

  • The date range shows today's date.

Step 10:

  • A Customer Invoice file downloads.

Step 11:

  • Line 1's ItemDescription cell is identical to the Description in cell A1: both routes cut the line at the same place.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 16 (27 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • S3-E3: “A description long enough to be cut still syncs. The invoice reaches QuickBooks; it does not land in Unexported Items.”
  • S3-R7: “When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.”
  • S3-R4: “The same text is used by the live QuickBooks sync and by the downloadable Customer Invoice report. Built at the same moment, the two never show different text for the same line, apart from the leading apostrophe the report adds in S3-R8a. An invoice already in QuickBooks keeps its old text there (S3-N1, S3-E4).”
  • Story 3, context note: “Context note on S3-R7: SV-9921 is the live example of the alternative. A value too long for a QuickBooks field put a customer's record in Unexported Items with a raw validation message that does not say which field failed.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.

References from Design

Design canvas "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Pz1Q6BfvreYFpQwVQZPTE6), copy re-read on 27 Oct 2026 (its one change since 13 Oct: the New Line board's "Title *" now reads "Title"): board 2.2 "The long end". These boards draw the line text, not a screen: the case types their example values where they fit; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • board-2.2-the-long-end.png

The design's own words:

  • “An accented character costs two bytes, so a cut at the 4,000th byte can land inside one and send a character broken in half. The rule now shortens from the end until the text fits and stops on a character boundary, so that cannot happen.”
